concepts.why: The patient presents with pain and swelling in the right mastoid area, a small amount of fluid in the right mastoid air cells, and mucosal thickening in the right ethmoid air cells, which are consistent with mastoiditis.
The patient has a hyperostotic lesion of the outer table of the right calvarium and thickening of the inner table, which are characteristic of hyperostosis.
The patient has a history of migraine disorder, which is a relevant factor in the diagnosis.
The patient has a densely calcified mass involving the inferior squamosal portion of the right temporal bone, which could be a bone tumor.
The patient presents with pain and swelling in the right mastoid area and a small amount of fluid in the right mastoid air cells, which are consistent with chronic otitis media.
The patient has a densely calcified mass involving the inferior squamosal portion of the right temporal bone, which is a temporal bone lesion.
It explains the hyperostotic lesion of the outer table of the right calvarium without intracranial extension or adjacent soft-tissue mass.

rationales.F02: Pain and swelling in the right mastoid area could be indicative of mastoiditis or a bone tumor in the temporal region.
rationales.F04: The presence of a hyperostotic lesion is a strong indicator of hyperostosis or a bone tumor.

rationales.F10: The presence of fluid in the mastoid air cells is a strong indicator of mastoiditis or chronic otitis media.
